chunks: And in the narration of ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, he said:
A man from the Anṣār came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I would like you to bear witness for me concerning date-palms that I have given to my son.”
He said: “Do you have any child other than him?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then have you given them as you have given him?” He said: “No.”
He said: “Indeed, we, the company of Prophets, do not bear witness to unfair deviation.”

key_terms.نَحَلْتُهَا: I gave it as a gift
key_terms.ٱلْأَنْصَارِ: the Helpers of Madinah from among the Prophet’s supporters
key_terms.ٱلْجَنَفِ: inclination from justice, unfair bias, or wrongful partiality

ai.seo_question: Can a parent single out one child with a gift and ask for testimony over it?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that preferential gifting to one child over others is a form of unfairness that should not be endorsed. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم refused to testify to such an act, showing the importance of justice among one's children and integrity in legal testimony.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3349 - In a narration from Abdullah ibn Maymun from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), it is stated:
"A man from the Ansar came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said:
'O Messenger of Allah (swt), I wish for you to bear witness for me regarding a palm grove that I have gifted to my son.'
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked: 'Do you have any children besides him?' He replied: 'Yes.'
The Prophet (sw) then asked: 'Did you gift them as you gifted him?'
He said: 'No.'
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, we, the community of Prophets, do not bear witness to bias (janaf).'"
